analysis.title: Walmart Inc. F3Q'27 Review - Largely In-Line Results Against A High Bar
key_insights: RBC rates WMT Outperform with an unchanged $131 price target, based on about 40x its revised FY'28 adjusted EPS estimate of $3.23. The firm calls the F3Q'27 results solid but says investors were largely already there.

Walmart US comp rose +2.9% in 3Q, up from +2.6% in 2Q. Grocery was up mid-single digits, general merchandise up low-single digits, and health and wellness down low-single digits including a roughly 8pt MFP headwind.

Management said it is seeing the highest level of market share gains in 3 years. RBC reads this as evidence that tariff-related price investment resonated with the consumer, and notes higher retention of share gains over the past few years.
Management said 4Q is off to a strong start and that rollbacks slowed from 11,200 in 2Q to 7,700 in 3Q.

Walmart US gross margin expanded about 50 bps y/y to 28.1%. Management attributed roughly 75 (units not stated in the source) of the y/y improvement to advertising, with most of the rest from the mix impact of MFP.
Walmart US advertising grew +37% y/y, the 7th consecutive quarter of 30%+ growth. Management said it has not scratched the surface on Vizio and Vibe.co.

WMT said e-commerce is approaching break-even excluding advertising, helped by densification (e-commerce penetration about 25%) and cost efficiencies. Forward deployment of marketplace inventory in stores is being piloted in a couple hundred stores ahead of the holidays. Automated DCs serve about 68-70% of stores.

RBC says it is probable that 4Q gross margin steps down from 3Q. Enterprise gross margin rose about 30 bps y/y in 3Q on mix and the BBD timing shift, partly offset by Sam's Club fuel margins. RBC assumes a good portion of the $650M carryover tariff refunds was used to offset higher fuel costs rather than reinvested in price.

RBC's baseline for 4Q is higher fuel costs q/q with less of a cost offset, and a roughly 5-10 bps negative impact from BBD. Advertising and MFP mix should remain a consistent tailwind q/q. RBC says it is unclear whether prices will creep higher in 4Q.

The WMT+/Sam's Club membership bundle is expected to be accretive to the enterprise. Management cautioned it will weigh on Sam's Club operating income growth until the program anniversaries in Oct '27, because membership income is split with Walmart US.

Early bundle metrics: a couple million new Sam's Club members in the first few weeks, WMT+ membership up double digits, Sam's Club app downloads up 20% since launch, and bundled members' online spend with WMT up more than 80% versus pre-launch.
The Flipkart Big Billion Days shift out of 3Q and into 4Q is a roughly 100 bps headwind to 3Q cc net sales growth and reverses as a roughly 100 bps tailwind in 4Q.
Management confirmed there are no remaining tariff refunds to deploy in 4Q.

MFP was a roughly 125 bps headwind to Walmart US comp in 3Q, partly offset by about 60 bps from GLP-1 sales. Management guided the MFP headwind next year to be at or slightly above this year's, while the GLP-1 benefit rolls off.

WMT now expects $2B+ of incremental fuel-related costs in FY'27 above its original guidance assumptions, and assumes fuel prices persist at current rates. Management also flagged a roughly 20 bps headwind to FY27 operating income growth from Vibe acquisition and integration costs.
At current exchange rates, management expects a 70 bps benefit to FY sales growth and a 130 bps benefit to operating income growth, with a net neutral FX effect in F4Q.

RBC keeps its 4Q Walmart US comp estimate at +3.1%. It trims 4Q cc net sales growth from +6.0% to +5.8% (FX) and 4Q adjusted EPS from $0.81 to $0.80 (higher fuel). FY'27/FY'28 Walmart US comp is now +3.2%/+3.3%, cc net sales +5.2%/+4.5%, and adjusted EPS $2.91/$3.23.

Valuation: the 40x multiple screens expensive against history, but RBC argues the business model has changed toward advertising and membership income. It uses COST and AMZN, which historically traded at 30x+, as better comps.

market_movers.rationale: RBC keeps Outperform and the $131 target (40x FY'28 adjusted EPS of $3.23) after F3Q'27. It cites share gains, advertising growth and near-breakeven e-commerce, weighed against higher fuel costs and Sam's Club membership accounting.

earnings_insights: WMT F3Q'27 (reported 11/19/2026 per RBC's review): Walmart US comp +2.9% ex-fuel vs +2.6% in 2Q. RBC's model shows 3Q EPS of $0.65 (+4.3% y/y) on net sales of $188.8B (+5.2% y/y). The report does not state consensus, and it calls the results largely in-line against a high bar.
RBC 4Q (Jan-27) estimates, all estimates not reported: net sales $202.5B (prior $202.4B), adjusted EPS $0.80 (prior $0.81), Walmart US comp +3.1%, cc net sales growth +5.8% (prior +6.0%).
RBC FY'27E estimates: revenue $757.0B (prior $756.2B), EPS $2.91 (prior $2.92), P/E 43.2x. FY'28E: revenue $790.5B (prior $788.8B), EPS $3.23 (unchanged), P/E 39.0x.
RBC FY'27 Walmart US comp +3.2% (prior +3.2%) and FY'28 +3.3% (prior +3.0%). cc net sales growth FY'27/FY'28 is +5.2%/+4.5% (prior +5.3%/+4.4%).

Walmart US gross margin of 28.1% in 3Q was up about 50 bps y/y. Enterprise gross margin was up about 30 bps y/y, helped by advertising mix and the BBD timing shift and partly offset by Sam's Club fuel margins.
RBC's 3Q model shows operating income of $7,770M (+7.0% y/y) and a gross profit margin of 24.5% (+28 bps y/y).

Guidance items from management: $2B+ of incremental FY'27 fuel costs above original assumptions, a roughly 20 bps FY27 operating income growth headwind from Vibe, and an FX benefit of 70 bps to FY sales growth and 130 bps to operating income growth at current rates.

macro_indicators.reading: WMT expects $2B+ of incremental fuel-related costs in FY'27 above original guidance assumptions
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher fuel costs weigh on Walmart's 4Q margin. RBC assumes fuel prices persist at current rates and cuts 4Q EPS from $0.81 to $0.80.
Food inflation was consistent q/q and supported the mid-single-digit grocery comp.
General merchandise inflation was consistent q/q, so general merchandise growth was mostly volume.

risk_factors: Consumer health and sentiment: an increase in fuel prices or job losses could reduce spending, including on the discretionary items that make up part of Walmart's mix (about 55% of sales are grocery).
Digital competition from existing competitors and online-only players like Amazon, and online investments that may continue to weigh on profitability.
Margin pressure from inflation across the supply chain. If Walmart cannot mitigate cost headwinds, RBC expects the shares to come under pressure.
4Q gross margin likely steps down from 3Q on higher fuel costs, a roughly 5-10 bps BBD impact, and uncertainty over whether prices rise.
Sam's Club operating income growth is pressured near term by the WMT+ membership bundle accounting until the program anniversaries in Oct '27.
MFP headwind to Walmart US comp is expected to be at or slightly above this year's next year, while the GLP-1 benefit rolls off.
Concern that tariff refund investments were bought sales at risk of disappearing when rollbacks end. RBC views higher retention of share gains as easing this.
geopolitical: Tariff-related price investment and carryover tariff refunds: management confirmed there are no remaining refunds to deploy in 4Q. Rollbacks have slowed from 11,200 to 7,700.

tension_points.bull_case: Advertising (+37% y/y) and MFP mix drove most of the roughly 50 bps Walmart US gross margin gain. RBC says both should remain consistent tailwinds q/q, and e-commerce is near breakeven excluding advertising.
tension_points.bear_case: RBC says 4Q gross margin probably steps down from 3Q on higher fuel costs, a roughly 5-10 bps BBD impact and rollbacks slowing as tariff refunds are used up. The Sam's Club membership bundle also pressures Sam's Club operating income growth until Oct '27.
tension_points.what_invalidates: RBC's downside scenario of $104 assumes consumer demand for general merchandise stays soft, food disinflation or deflation weighs on grocery sales, and tariffs dull profitability.

theme_stances.key_argument: Highest share gains in 3 years show tariff-related price investment resonated with the consumer, and advertising keeps lifting gross margin.
theme_stances.evidence: highest level of share gains they've seen in 3 years
